title: Read a driver from the tree, read-only
prompt:
# Story 3: Read a driver from the tree, read-only

- **Story**: XXX-read-driver-from-builder
- **Created**: 2026-11-07
- **Status**: Draft
- **Demo**: open `drivers`, press `constraints.md`, read it rendered and as Markdown, see that nothing can be changed, show the files again,
  and close it.

## Story

As a team member, I want to open a driver from the tree and read it, rendered or as Markdown, so that I can see what steers my project
without leaving the builder, knowing that I cannot change it there.

## Acceptance tests

Opening

- [ ] **Given** `drivers` is open, **When** the user presses a driver file, **Then** the file opens in a panel that takes the area to the right
  of the tree, its row in the tree shows as selected (`aria-current`), and its folder stays open.
- [ ] **Given** a file is open, **Then** the tree shrinks to a thin rail: a "Show files" button, a thin line, and the icon of the kind of
  file that is open (labelled "Viewing a file from drivers", tooltip "drivers").
- [ ] **Given** the rail, **When** the user presses "Show files", **Then** the full tree is beside the file again. **When** the user picks
  another file in it, **Then** that file opens and the tree is a rail again.
- [ ] **Given** a file is open, **When** the user presses the same file in the tree, **Then** nothing changes. **When** the user presses another
  driver, **Then** it takes the place of the first.

The panel

- [ ] **Given** the open file, **Then** the header shows the driver icon, the path `drivers/constraints.md` in monospace (cut with "...", and
  complete as a tooltip), a lock with "Read-only here. Edit this driver from the Drivers page.", and a Close button named "Close
  drivers/constraints.md".
- [ ] **Given** the panel, **Then** it has no Save, Delete, Sync, "Add link", "Add task", diagram or UI button, no field that can be typed in,
  and no "Cross enabler" button.
- [ ] **Given** the panel, **Then** two icon buttons choose how the text shows: the rendered text (selected when the file opens) and the
  Markdown source.
- [ ] **Given** the rendered view, **Then** headings, paragraphs, lists, bold, italic, code, quotes, tables and links show as such. A link to a
  safe address opens in a new tab; any other address shows only its text.
- [ ] **Given** the Markdown view, **Then** the source shows as plain text in a block, with long lines wrapped, and it cannot be edited. The
  user can still select and copy it.
- [ ] **Given** a driver with text, **Then** the Markdown is `# <name>`, the meaning of the driver (the fixed ones only) and the text. **Given**
  a driver with no text, **Then** the text reads "Not written yet. Edit this driver from the Drivers page." (in italics when rendered).
- [ ] **Given** the user changed the driver on the Drivers page and opened the workspace again, **Then** the file shows the saved text.
- [ ] **Given** the user switches between the two views and then opens another file, **Then** the new file opens rendered.

Closing

- [ ] **Given** the open file, **When** the user presses Close, **Then** the panel closes, the tree is full again, the empty state shows again
  ("Select a file in the tree to read it."), and the folders that were open still are.

## Business rules and constraints

- A driver is immutable here. It is written on the Drivers page, and the file view never writes to it: there is no editing, saving, renaming,
  moving or deleting from the builder.
- What shows is the saved text, never a draft of the Drivers page.
- The file view for a driver shows its text and nothing else: the links between documents ("Linked to" and "Referenced by") come with the
  stories and the enablers.
- The text is read and rendered by BWYN's own small Markdown reader, which builds elements and never HTML, so text that came from a repository
  cannot add markup.

## Out of scope

- Opening an ADR (story 4), and anything about stories and architectural enablers.
- Editing a driver, a link from the file to the Drivers page, and the links between documents.
- Copying the path, downloading the file, and printing.

## Tasks

- [ ] Open a file from a row of the tree: remember which is open, mark its row, keep its folder open, and shrink the tree to the rail (and
  back with "Show files").
- [ ] Build the file panel for a read-only file: icon, path, lock and note per kind, Close button, and nothing that edits.
- [ ] Add the two views, rendered and Markdown source, and open every file rendered.
- [ ] Build the driver's Markdown from its name, its meaning and its text, with the "Not written yet" line for an empty one.
- [ ] Close the file back to the empty state, with the tree full and its folders as they were.
- [ ] Leave the "Linked to" and "Referenced by" sections, the task, diagram, UI, sync and delete controls and the link picker out of the file
  panel.
- [ ] Test: open, switch, show files, close, both views, a driver with text and one without, and that no control edits.

## Files of the spike

In `bwyn-frontend/spikes/home-page/`. These are the base for the stories. The spike's workspace does much more than these stories ask
for (see the next section), so each file is used in part.

| File | What it holds | Stories |

## What the spike does that these stories take out or change

- **The middle of the workspace is the prompt.** In the spike, `ChatPanel` fills it, with the chat, the draft and the buttons that create
  stories and enablers. These stories put an empty state there ("Select a file in the tree to read it."). With a file open, the spike shows
  the file on the left and the prompt on the right (a 26 rem column); here the file takes the whole width.
- **The tree header has two buttons**: the runway diagram and "New story". Both are taken out.
- **The tree has more than four folders' worth of rows.** Under `stories` it has themes (create, rename with double click or F2, drag and
  drop, a runway button each), story folders and their file. All of that is taken out. `architectural-enablers` shows its files in the
  spike, and opening them offers editing, links, sync and delete: here it shows "Coming in another story." instead.
- **Folders start open in the spike**: `DEFAULT_EXPANDED` is `stories` and `enablers`. Here all four start closed, since the two that were
  open are inert.
- **The file panel of a driver or an ADR is the same component as a story's**, with the editing parts hidden by `entry.editable`. In the
  spike it also shows "Linked to" and "Referenced by" when something links to the file. Here those are left out until stories and enablers
  exist.
- **The breadcrumb ends with "Prompt"** while the workspace is open. Here it ends with "Files".

## Spike details worth keeping in mind

- The folder keys in the spike are `drivers`, `adrs`, `enablers` (for `architectural-enablers`) and `stories`.
- `buildEntries` gives each driver the file name `<identity>.md` and the label of its name; each ADR its stored `fileName` and the label
  `ADR 0011. <title>`; both `editable: false` and `links: []`.
- Opening a file makes `treeCollapsed` true unless `treeForced` is set by "Show files". Opening another file from the full tree clears
  `treeForced`, so the rail returns.
- `perform` opens the folder of the file that is opened, so a file opened from a link elsewhere (in later stories) shows in its folder.
- Choosing "Builder" in the menu while the workspace is open does nothing: only another item closes it (`setBuilderOpen(false)`), and the
  Builder page appears only after going away and coming back.
- Changing the project keeps `builderOpen`, and `BuilderWorkspace` is keyed by project, so it opens again on the new project with its state
  reset.
- The count of a folder is `entries.filter(kind).length`. For `drivers` that is always at least five.
- A driver written as Markdown is `# <name>`, the meaning, and the text, or `_Not written yet. Edit this driver from the Drivers page._`.
- The rendered view builds React elements from the Markdown and has a message "Nothing written yet." for a file with no blocks, which a driver
  or an ADR never reaches.
- Everything is read from the browser's storage in the spike, per project, so the workspace shows what the Drivers and ADR pages saved there.

tasks.text: Add open-file state to the workspace: track which entry is open, mark its tree row `aria-current`, keep its folder open, and collapse the tree to the rail on open.
Build the rail: "Show files" button, separator, and kind icon with label and tooltip; restore the full tree on "Show files" and return to the rail when a new file is chosen from the full tree.
Build the read-only file panel shell: driver icon, truncated path with tooltip, lock note, and Close button; wire Close to clear the open-file state and restore the full tree.
Enforce read-only: confirm the panel contains no Save, Delete, Sync, "Add link", "Add task", diagram, UI, "Cross enabler" button, or editable field.
Add the rendered/source toggle: default to rendered on every file open; switch to source on demand; reset to rendered when a new file opens.

Implement the Markdown renderer using React elements (no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`): headings, paragraphs, lists, bold, italic, inline code, block quotes, tables, and safe external links in a new tab.
Implement the Markdown source block: read-only, wrappable, selectable and copyable plain-text display.
Implement `driverMarkdown`: compose `# <name>`, the meaning line for fixed drivers, and the saved text; substitute the "Not written yet" italic placeholder when text is absent.
Read driver text from the project store so the panel always reflects the last saved state from the Drivers page.
Show the empty state "Select a file in the tree to read it." when no file is open; restore it and the pre-open folder state on Close.

Write Jest tests covering: opening a driver, switching files, the rail and "Show files" toggle, closing, both views, a driver with text, a driver without text, and the absence of any editable control in the panel.
